name: sse2neon
desc: Translator from Intel SSE intrinsics to Arm/Aarch64 NEON implementation
why: Translates Intel SSE intrinsics into ARM NEON, a neat look at how SIMD instructions map across architectures.

brief.what_it_is: sse2neon is a C/C++ header file, sse2neon.h, that provides NEON-based implementations of Intel SSE intrinsics. You copy the header into a project and replace the x86 includes (xmmintrin.h, emmintrin.h and so on) with it, so code written against SSE intrinsics compiles for little-endian Arm and AArch64. It covers MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2 and AES. Some intrinsics map to one NEON instruction, while others, such as _mm_maddubs_epi16 at 22 instructions, need several.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as enabling rapid porting of x86 SIMD code to Arm platforms while preserving the original semantics of the SSE intrinsics.
brief.how_it_works: It is a single header that supplies its own versions of the SSE function names, built on Arm NEON intrinsics, so the calling code does not change. Some results differ from SSE because NEON trades IEEE-754 compliance for speed on denormals and NaNs. Compile-time macros such as SSE2NEON_PRECISE_MINMAX or SSE2NEON_PRECISE_SQRT, defined as 1 before the include, switch to slower and more precise implementations. The example given is _mm_rsqrt_ps, which returns NaN for 0.0 on NEON where SSE returns INF.

brief.install_notes: There is no package-manager install in the README. Copy sse2neon.h into your source tree and include it in place of the SSE headers. Add the -march or -mfpu flag for your target. Requirements: little-endian ARM only (big-endian gives a compile-time error); GCC 10+, Clang 11+, MSVC 2019+ (v142) with ARM64 and ARM64EC targets, or Apple Clang 12+. Earlier GCC and Clang versions have vector codegen bugs. On Windows ARM64EC, the header skips <intrin.h> automatically. Testing needs make, and QEMU for cross-compiled runs on non-Arm hosts. Memory from _mm_malloc() must be freed with _mm_free().
brief.standout: It is a single drop-in header whose behaviour is tuned per use case: the README gives a table of which precision flags to enable for graphics, DSP, crypto, scientific, game physics and ML workloads, with the defaults chosen for speed. The README also documents the NEON-versus-SSE divergences openly, including the MONITOR/MWAIT policy, where _mm_monitor is a no-op and _mm_mwait maps to yield, wfe or wfi.
brief.status: unknown. The fetched README has GitHub Actions and coverage badges and a long list of adopters, but it shows no release version, release date or last commit date, so I could not confirm recent activity. I did not fetch the commit history or the releases page.
brief.caveats: Little-endian ARM only. Earlier GCC and Clang versions produce wrong vector code for some intrinsics. Default settings trade IEEE-754 accuracy for speed, so NaN, denormal and reciprocal results can differ from SSE unless the SSE2NEON_PRECISE_* flags are set. The README notes that some divergences (FTZ/DAZ, NaN payloads) cannot be fully removed. Optimization levels such as -O1 and -O2 may break code that changes rounding modes or calls _MM_SET_DENORMALS_ZERO_MODE() repeatedly. The __m128 type is not ABI-compatible with x64 code under ARM64EC. Memory from _mm_malloc must not be freed with free(), which corrupts the heap on Windows. Licensed under the MIT License.
quotes: A C/C++ header file that converts Intel SSE intrinsics to Arm/Aarch64 NEON intrinsics.
NEON trades IEEE-754 compliance for performance when handling denormals and NaNs.
All precision flags are disabled by default to maximize performance.
Big-endian ARM is not supported and will produce a compile-time error.

judge.reason: A compact, inspectable map from SSE semantics to NEON exposes both instruction expansion and floating-point mismatches, making this more than routine portability glue.

entry.title: sse2neon
entry.tldr: A single C header that lets x86 SSE intrinsic code compile on Arm by re-implementing each SSE call with NEON, showing how SIMD maps across architectures.
entry.deeper_look:
sse2neon is one header, `sse2neon.h`. You swap the x86 includes (`xmmintrin.h`, `emmintrin.h` and friends) for it, and code written against SSE intrinsics compiles for little-endian Arm and AArch64. It covers MMX, SSE, SSE2, SSE3, SSSE3, SSE4.1, SSE4.2 and AES. The README frames the goal as rapid porting of x86 SIMD code to Arm while preserving the original semantics.

The interesting part is reading how the mapping works. Some intrinsics become a single NEON instruction. Others need many: `_mm_maddubs_epi16` takes 22 instructions. The two instruction sets were not designed to match, so every function in the header is a small answer to the question of how to get the same result on different hardware.

The edges are where it gets honest. NEON trades IEEE-754 compliance for speed on denormals and NaNs, so some results differ from SSE. The README's example is `_mm_rsqrt_ps`, which returns NaN for 0.0 on NEON where SSE returns INF. Macros such as `SSE2NEON_PRECISE_MINMAX` and `SSE2NEON_PRECISE_SQRT`, defined as 1 before the include, switch to slower and more precise versions. The README also includes a table of which flags suit graphics, DSP, crypto, scientific, game physics and ML work.
entry.install: There is no package-manager install in the README, and the brew formula installs no executables. Copy `sse2neon.h` into your source tree and include it in place of the SSE headers. Add the flag for your target, such as `-march=armv8-a+fp+simd+crypto+crc` for AArch64. Needs GCC 10+, Clang 11+, MSVC 2019+ or Apple Clang 12+, on little-endian Arm. Running the tests needs `make`, plus QEMU on non-Arm hosts.

entry.whats_unique: It is a drop-in single header that documents openly where NEON and SSE diverge, and lets you choose speed or precision per workload with compile-time flags.
entry.caveats: Little-endian Arm only, older GCC and Clang have vector codegen bugs, default settings trade IEEE-754 accuracy for speed, and the brief could not confirm recent project activity.
